item.title: (De-)Capitalisation of Export Credit Insurance Premiums
item.description:
The Challenge

Insurance policies frequently need to be amended during their lifetime. Changes to a financing structure, repayment schedule, insured amount or cover ratio can result in either a premium surcharge or a premium refund. In some cases, the economic effect of this adjustment is transmitted into the underlying financing transaction: a surcharge is capitalised into the insured credit amount, while a refund can be used to further reduce outstanding insured capital.

item.title: Dealing with the Non-Marketable: Export Credit Insurances
item.description:
The Challenge

Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) insure risks that commercial insurers avoid: long-term, high-risk, and often politically uncertain transactions. While pricing export credit insurance policies is already complex, pricing modifications to these policies is an even greater challenge. There are no regulatory guidelines, no established market benchmarks, and each export case exhibits unique characteristics and therefore idiosyncratic risk profiles.
